synthesis.description: Schedulers and volume staff path deal volumes to contracts and meters in the scheduling systems and link buybacks to the market deals they offset. Rounds start when a buyback is announced, when a monthly path list is sent out for checking, when a storage customer needs a specific withdrawal path, or when one scheduler changes a path another created. Questions about pricing, documentation from the counterparty and whether a buyback exists at all go back and forth until the supply and market deals are attached as a buy/sell and the month's activity is reviewed.
steps: Receive notice of a sale, buyback or pathing requirement from the desk or a customer.
Confirm the deal terms, pricing type and counterparty documentation.
Create or change the path in the scheduling system for the meter and volume.
Attach the supply deal to the market deal to establish the buy/sell or buyback link.
Circulate the monthly path list for others to check for anything out of line.
Review the month's allocations, links and buybacks and correct what is wrong.
synthesis.approach: A validation report that compares each month's paths against active deals, flags buybacks with no linked market deal, flags path edits made by someone other than the creator, and lists deals with tiered pricing, so the monthly path list arrives pre-checked. A short procedure fixes who links buybacks and who confirms counterparty documentation.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are a check of whether paths and buyback links match the deals. A checklist for the monthly review, covering links, buybacks, pricing type and documentation, gives schedulers one shared standard and reduces the disagreements and ownership questions the mail shows.
